record.paper_title: Trimer Covers in the Triangular Grid: Twenty Mostly Open Problems
record.original_question: Let T113(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3; 3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

evidence.quote: Let Tijk (a, b; 3) denote the weighted sum of the i, j, k tilings of the (a, b)-benzel as defined near the end of section 1, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m.
Problem 18: Is T113 (n, 2n - 3; 3) 2-adically continuous as a function of n >= 4?
The sequence appears to be constant mod 2, constant mod 4, 2-periodic mod 8, and 8-periodic mod 16.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the triangular grid, regarded as a tiling of the plane by unit equilateral triangles colored alternately up-pointing and down-pointing. A "cell" is a triangle of this grid. A "stone" is the union of three pairwise-adjacent cells (i.e., three cells meeting at a vertex; there are two orientations, one with two up-cells and one down-cell, the other with two down-cells and one up-cell). A "bone" is the union of three contiguous collinear cells; there are three orientations of bones, corresponding to the three possible axis directions.

For positive integers a, b, the (a,b)-benzel is a certain hexagonally symmetric region in the triangular grid (defined as follows: take the regular hexagon centered at the origin whose vertices in some coordinate system are determined by a and b, and remove the three "corner" up-triangles in a prescribed way so that the resulting region admits trimer covers). A trimer cover (or tiling) of the (a,b)-benzel is a partition of its cells into stones and bones.

Define
$$T_{113}(a,b;3) := \sum_{\tau} 3^{m(\tau)},$$
where the sum runs over all tilings τ of the (a,b)-benzel using both orientations of stones and all three orientations of bones, and m(τ) denotes the number of stones in τ.

For each integer n ≥ 4, the value T₁₁₃(n, 2n−3; 3) is a well-defined non-negative integer. Recall that a function f : ℤ≥N → ℤ is said to be 2-adically continuous if for every integer k ≥ 1 there exists an integer M ≥ 1 such that whenever m ≡ n (mod 2^M), one has f(m) ≡ f(n) (mod 2^k); equivalently, f extends to a continuous function on the 2-adic integers.

Question: Is the sequence n ↦ T₁₁₃(n, 2n−3; 3), n ≥ 4, 2-adically continuous?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as one of twenty mostly open problems on trimer covers of benzel regions posed by Propp (2022). Searches reveal subsequent work on benzel tilings (e.g., generalized compression methods and nearly symmetric hexagons with holes by Lai) but no resolution of this specific 2-adic continuity problem for weighted T₁₁₃(n, 2n−3; 3). The empirical observation that the sequence is constant mod 2, constant mod 4, 2-periodic mod 8, and 8-periodic mod 16 remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Trimer covers in the triangular grid: twenty mostly open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Propp poses twenty mostly open problems about trimer covers of benzel regions, including weighted enumerations T_{ijk}(a,b;3) and conjectured 2-adic continuity properties.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in Propp's list.

status_evidence.title: Propp's benzels and Lai's nearly symmetric hexagons with holes
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work addresses some benzel-tiling problems via bijective and product formulas, but does not resolve the 2-adic continuity question for T_{113}(n,2n-3;3).
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up papers on benzels do not resolve this specific 2-adic continuity question.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of benzels via generalized compression
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized compression techniques are used to prove some enumerative results on benzel tilings, but the weighted 2-adic continuity problem remains untreated.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature on benzels does not establish 2-adic continuity of T_{113}(n,2n-3;3).
